questions.question: What do flashing amber lights on a school warning sign mean?
options: Children are crossing or nearby, so slow down
questions.explain: Rule 208: flashing amber lights show that a school crossing or children are active ahead.

questions.question: What colour comes immediately after a single steady amber light?
questions.explain: Rule 175: in the UK sequence, green goes to amber, then to red.

questions.question: What flashing lights mark a UK zebra crossing?
options: Amber Belisha beacons on black-and-white poles
questions.explain: Rule 195: flashing amber Belisha beacons warn drivers of a zebra crossing ahead.

questions.question: What do yellow 'SCHOOL KEEP CLEAR' zig-zag lines outside a school mean?
options: Do not wait, stop, or park there
questions.explain: Rule 238: keep school entrance zig-zags clear so children and drivers can see each other.

questions.question: Where should you stop for someone on a zebra crossing?
questions.explain: Rule 195: stop behind the dashed line so pedestrians have the full width of the crossing.

questions.question: You see a ball bounce into the road near a school. What should you do?
options: Slow down and be ready to stop in case a child runs after it
questions.explain: Rule 208: a child may follow a ball into the road without looking.

questions.question: A car in the lane beside you stops at a zebra crossing. What should you do?
options: Stop too, as a pedestrian may be crossing out of sight
questions.explain: Rule 191: never overtake a vehicle stopped at a crossing; someone may be hidden behind it.

questions.question: What do the white zig-zag lines beside a pedestrian crossing mean?
options: You must not park or overtake there
You may park for five minutes
You must speed up past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking and overtaking within crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: When may you enter a yellow criss-cross box junction to go straight ahead?
options: Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when your exit road is clear
When the car ahead is still moving slowly
At any time if you signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 states you must not enter a box junction unless your exit is clear.

questions.question: At speeds up to 30 mph, how much side space should you leave when overtaking a cyclist?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists up to 30 mph.

questions.question: What minimum gap should you leave behind the car in front on a dry road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 sets at least a two-second gap in dry conditions.

questions.question: When should you give a signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: In good time before you make the move
Only when another car is behind you
Only at night or in rain
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 tells you to give clear signals in good time.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car in a built-up area with street lights, unless signed otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 30 mph as the standard built-up area limit for cars.

questions.question: What do red and amber lights showing together mean?
options: Also means stop; do not pass until green shows
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 175 says RED AND AMBER also means stop; you must wait for green.

questions.question: What do double broken white lines across the end of your road mean?
options: You have priority over cross traffic
Give way to traffic on the road you are joining
Stop for five seconds even if clear
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 says double broken lines mean give way to traffic on the main road.

questions.question: You are turning into a side road and a pedestrian is waiting to cross it. What should you do?
options: Sound your horn to warn them
Give way and let them cross
Speed up to clear the turn
Wave them to stay on the kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule H2 says you should give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road into which or from which you are turning.

questions.question: What must you check before changing lanes?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says you must check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which side of the road should you normally drive on in the UK?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 160 says you should keep to the left unless overtaking or turning right.

questions.question: At a UK roundabout, which traffic must you give way to?
options: Traffic approaching from your immediate right
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 says to give way to traffic approaching from your right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when turning left at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires signalling left on approach when taking the first exit.

questions.question: Why should you choose your roundabout approach lane early?
options: To avoid last-second swerving across other drivers
So you do not need signals
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 encourages early lane selection for smooth, safe driving.

questions.question: If you want to change lanes while circulating on a roundabout, what must you do first?
options: Check mirrors and blind spot, signal, and wait for a clear gap
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 133 require full checks before changing lanes.

questions.question: At a roundabout with three approach lanes, the middle lane is marked straight ahead. Which lane should you use to go straight?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to follow painted lane markings on multi-lane approaches.

questions.question: If you approach a roundabout in the wrong lane and traffic is beside you, what is safest?
options: Follow your lane safely and turn around later
Cut across the car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 avoids sudden lane changes across circulating traffic.

questions.question: When can the right-hand approach lane also be used for going straight ahead?
options: When road signs or lane arrows direct straight-ahead traffic into that lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 notes that signs and markings can override the default left lane.

questions.question: Who benefits most from a clear left exit signal on a roundabout?
options: Drivers waiting at the next entrance to join the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses exit signals to show waiting drivers you are leaving.

questions.question: At a painted mini-roundabout, how should you pass the white circle when turning right?
options: Drive clockwise around the painted circle if possible
Cut straight across the wrong side of the circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 188 and Rule 185 state all vehicles must pass around the central marking clockwise.

questions.question: You have already crossed the first white line when the light turns amber and you cannot stop safely there. What must you do?
options: Stop at the second white line
questions.explain: Rule 178 says if you cannot stop safely at the first line, stop at the second white line.

questions.question: The light is red, and there is a green left filter arrow lit. What may you do?
options: Turn left if safe, watching for pedestrians
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 177 allows you to move only in the direction of the green filter arrow.

questions.question: Why are STOP signs placed at certain junctions instead of Give Way signs?
options: Because the view of the main road is poor
questions.explain: Rule 171: sTOP signs are used where sightlines are restricted so drivers must stop and look carefully.

questions.question: What should you check in your mirrors just before signalling left to leave an inner roundabout lane?
options: Check your left mirror and blind spot for cars or cyclists beside you
Only look at the central island
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells you to watch for traffic on your left before moving out to exit.

questions.question: If you want to make a U-turn at a roundabout, how must you do it?
options: Turn right immediately before the island
Drive all the way around the island clockwise and exit back
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 shows you must travel clockwise around the roundabout to return.

questions.question: Why should you not stop inside the cycle box even if no cyclist is there yet?
options: Cyclists may ride up the left side to use it
questions.explain: Rule 178: cyclists filter forward to reach the box safely before the lights change.

questions.question: What if you accidentally stop with your front bumper over the white line on red?
options: Stop and wait there without entering the crossing or junction
questions.explain: Rule 175: never cross the junction on red; wait safely for green.

questions.question: What should you do if you realise you are in the wrong lane on a busy roundabout?
options: Follow your lane safely, take that exit, and turn around later
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 recommends staying safe in your lane rather than cutting across traffic.

questions.question: After stopping at the white line, you still cannot see clearly. What should you do?
options: Creep forward slowly until you can see
questions.explain: Rule 171: stop at the line first, then edge forward slowly to get a clear view before pulling out.

questions.question: Why is overtaking banned inside crossing zig-zag lines?
options: The overtaken car can hide a pedestrian stepping onto the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 protects pedestrians whose view of approaching cars is blocked.

questions.question: When are you allowed to stop inside a yellow box junction?
options: When turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic to clear
When queuing to go straight ahead
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 allows stopping in the box only when turning right and blocked by oncoming cars.

questions.question: What should you do if there is not enough room to pass a cyclist with 1.5 metres to spare?
options: Wait behind the cyclist until it is safe to pass wide
Flash your headlights until they mount the pavement
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to wait behind if you cannot leave enough room to overtake safely.

questions.question: Why is a fixed two-car-length gap unsafe at 70 mph?
options: Stopping distance grows sharply at high speed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 uses time rather than car lengths because stopping distance rises with speed.

questions.question: Two side roads are close together on your left and you want the second one. When should you signal?
options: As you pass the first side road
100 metres before the first side road
After turning into the second road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to signal before an earlier turning you are not taking.

questions.question: If you drive down a steep hill, what must you watch to stay within the limit?
options: Your speed can creep up without pressing the accelerator
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies downhill too; use gears and brakes to stay legal.

questions.question: If a vehicle on the main road is flashing its headlights at you, what should you assume?
options: It is always safe to pull out
Wait until you are sure the way is clear and safe
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 means you stay responsible for pulling out only when it is genuinely safe.

questions.question: In slow queuing traffic, when should you change lanes?
options: Whenever a tiny gap opens for a moment
Only when it is safe and you will not block others
As fast as possible before the queue stops
Without signalling so others do not speed up
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises not weaving between lanes or cutting across other drivers.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, three cars arrive at once and nobody has clear priority. What should you do?
options: Make eye contact, proceed slowly, and give way if unsure
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and courtesy advice help resolve deadlocks safely.

questions.question: Why is a right signal on approach helpful to drivers waiting at the left-hand entrance?
options: It warns them you are staying on the roundabout past their exit
It tells them to pull out in front of you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 helps waiting drivers judge whether you will cross their path.

questions.question: A driver behind flashes their lights after you signal left. What does your signal give you?
options: No right of way; wait until the move is safe
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 states signals never give you priority over anyone else.

questions.question: If a car is towing a trailer on a dual carriageway, does it share the 70 mph car limit?
options: No, towing vehicles have a lower 60 mph limit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets a 60 mph limit for cars towing trailers on dual carriageways.

questions.question: You see a car approaching from the right with its left indicator on. What should you do?
options: Wait until you are sure it is actually turning before pulling out
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 warns never to assume a flashing indicator means the driver will turn.

questions.question: In heavy rain, why do blind-spot checks matter even more before changing lanes?
options: Spray reduces what you can see in side mirrors
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and wet-weather advice warn that spray hides vehicles in mirrors.
